source_access_notes: Independently inspected Resuscitation Council UK 2025 adult and paediatric life support and first-aid guidance, NHS fainting guidance, and Italian CdS art.189. Child BLS initial breaths differ from adult BLS; airway access remains priority with suspected neck injury. 31602 consciousness alone does not settle need for neurological assessment; evidence does not claim official intended meaning.

Rechecked corrections: CPR trigger includes both unresponsiveness and abnormal breathing; adult compression-first and trained paediatric initial five rescue breaths distinguish RCUK 2025 sequences, with dispatcher guidance for all. Age-neutral rows avoid imposing adult sequence on children.

issues.reason: Il quesito dichiara falso che, se cosciente, si debba verificare il movimento coordinato degli arti, senza specificare che tale controllo serva a determinare la coscienza. Le linee guida contemplano valutazioni motorie neurologiche in alcune situazioni; non è verificata una regola generale che renda falsa l’affermazione così formulata. Serve adjudicazione del contesto inteso rispetto al verdetto stampato.

issues.reason: CPR instruction is triggered by abnormal breathing without explicitly requiring unresponsiveness; an alert person in respiratory distress must not receive chest compressions. Include unresponsiveness and do not delay emergency call/CPR to inspect.

31610 and 31611 give adult compression-first sequence and optional breaths without age scope. RCUK 2025 paediatric BLS specifies five initial breaths for paediatric BLS; untrained rescuers follow dispatcher. Scope the adult sequence and include concise child/dispatcher qualification; assess 31606 and 31623 where an explicit compression-first instruction also appears.

source_access_notes: Independently inspected Resuscitation Council UK 2025 adult and paediatric life support and first-aid guidance, NHS fainting guidance, and Italian CdS art.189. Child BLS initial breaths differ from adult BLS; airway access remains priority with suspected neck injury. 31602 consciousness alone does not settle need for neurological assessment; evidence does not claim official intended meaning.
